name: Anarcho-primitivism
summary: Anarcho-primitivism is an anarchist critique of civilization as a whole. It holds that the shift from foraging to agriculture and domestication brought hierarchy, coercion, alienation and ecological destruction, and that the state, work, the division of labor and industrial technology all grow from that turn. Adherents want civilization dismantled and people to live in small, egalitarian, face-to-face communities modelled loosely on hunter-gatherer bands, in close contact with nature.
scope: The North American anti-civilization current of the 1980s to today, chiefly John Zerzan (Future Primitive and later writings), John Moore's A Primitivist Primer and Fredy Perlman, within the green anarchist milieu. It excludes Ted Kaczynski's non-anarchist anti-tech revolution, Rousseau and other earlier primitivist philosophers, and social ecology or other green anarchisms that keep technology and agriculture.

sources.usedFor: Scholarly summary: return to a pre-civilized past, critique of the technological state

universal-healthcare.rationale: State provision depends on the state and on industrial medicine, both of which primitivists want gone; Zerzan expects health to come from removing civilization's causes of illness instead.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred: wage policy reforms work rather than abolishing it, and primitivists dismiss such reforms as leaving daily life under civilization intact.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Primitivists want production and the economy as categories to lose their meaning and call for abolishing globalization, so they reject markets as the allocator.

public-ownership.rationale: They oppose both the state that would own these industries and the industrial systems themselves, which they want dismantled.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and anti-reformism: redistribution by state taxation leaves civilization's structures in place.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred: unions organize workers within work and industry, while primitivists reject work itself and dismiss leftist organizations as power-seeking rackets.

property-fundamental.rationale: Zerzan holds that foragers lacked private property and proposes abolishing it; property and poverty are treated as inventions of civilization.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: tighter state regulation is the reformism primitivists reject, since they want the industrial system abolished, not managed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its apparatus abolished but do not take up welfare's work incentives; the dependency framing is outside their critique, so they are indifferent.

worker-ownership.rationale: Self-managed production keeps work and the division of labor, which Moore says classical anarchism and Marxism would merely rework rather than abolish.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The movement aims to end structures of control and coercion and to abolish the state's administrative and security apparatus.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state coercion over individuals; primitivist texts do not address drug law.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state law and coercion; primitivists do not discuss speech law, and some also distrust language itself.

strong-leader.rationale: Primitivism aims to end all power relations; concentrated personal rule is the opposite of the egalitarian band society it holds up.

state-harmful.rationale: As a branch of anarchism, primitivism calls for abolishing the state together with the civilization that produced it.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: state licensing is a form of control primitivists oppose, though guns are industrial products and the texts do not address them.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moore calls for abolishing the state's administrative and military apparatus, and Zerzan ties organized violence to civilization.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Anti-statism argues against criminal bans, but the critique of commodification and the objectification of women argues against the trade; the texts do not settle it.

decide-locally.rationale: Zerzan wants radically decentralized, face-to-face communities modelled on band society instead of mass society.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject the punitive state altogether, so of the two aims they would favour the less coercive one, though they want no prisons at all.

traditional-family.rationale: Zerzan links patriarchy to domestication, and Moore looks to women freed of gender constraints and the family structure.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism and the critique of the patriarchal family; marriage law as such is not discussed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state control and Moore's view that women should not be defined by reproduction; abortion is not discussed directly.

more-religion-public.rationale: Zerzan lists religion among the products of domestication and sees ritual and shamans as early sources of domination.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Primitivists side with peoples harmed by civilization's expansion, but state remedy programs are the reform they reject; the texts do not address it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Zerzan argues foragers had flexible roles and relative sexual equality, with gender hierarchy arising from domestication, and Moore speaks of gender constraints to be shed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nations and their symbolic cultures belong to the civilization primitivists want undone, and they treat symbolic culture as a source of alienation.

gradual-change.rationale: Zerzan calls for a sudden, uncompromising break, saying half a revolution would only preserve domination, and Moore rejects reformism.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred: immigration control is exercised by the states primitivists want abolished.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Global governance extends the mass society and globalization that Zerzan wants abolished.

free-trade.rationale: Zerzan calls for the abolition of globalization and sees industrial production as the engine of ecological destruction.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject nation-states and nationalism, though they are equally hostile to international institutions.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: They want military apparatus abolished and see organized warfare as a product of civilization.

open-borders.rationale: Borders presuppose the states primitivists want abolished, and band societies did not hold fixed territory against outsiders.

limit-growth.rationale: Primitivists treat civilization's expansion as leading toward an uninhabitable earth and want industrial production dismantled.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: They see the ecological crisis as dire but regard government programs as reforms that keep industrial civilization going; climate policy is inferred, not discussed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technology is seen as the root of alienation and the Leviathan's armory, and Zerzan says the system's tools cannot build a liberated world.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear power is a large-scale technological system of the kind Moore says demands obedience, and primitivists want such systems dismantled.

revolution-justified.rationale: Zerzan calls for a sudden total break and says industrial society needs to be destroyed, and Moore speaks of insurgency; pacifist primitivists dissent on force.

experts-over-public.rationale: Specialization and the division of labor are core targets of the primitivist critique, which ties them to the rise of hierarchy.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning combines the state, mass society and industrial production, all of which primitivists want abolished.

socialized-markets.rationale: Primitivists reject both markets and production for exchange; collective ownership of firms is the reformism Moore criticizes.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred: it relies on state taxation and land ownership, both alien to the band society primitivists favour.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from anti-statism: primitivists want property abolished, not taxed by a state.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred: a state money payment keeps both the state and the money economy primitivists want gone.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Primitivists oppose globalization but want industry dismantled, not shielded; the statement's goal of protecting industry runs against them.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Industrial policy expands both the state and industrial production, which primitivists want abolished.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Primitivists see property itself as an invention of civilization, so dispersing it among small owners is not their aim.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Zerzan opposes the coercion of work and wants production and economy to lose their meaning, citing sharing foragers without property.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: They would end central banks along with the state, but reject leaving money to the market, since money itself should go.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies managing wages and prices expand both state power and the economy of work primitivists reject.

one-party-rule.rationale: Moore dismisses parties and organizations as rackets for putting an ideology in power, and the movement aims to abolish power, not capture it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kings and priests are presented as the original agents of civilized exploitation and hierarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Moore rejects politics as government and Zerzan is anti-leftist; representative democracy is a form of state rule over mass society.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred: they prefer face-to-face self-rule over representation, though referendums within a state are not their model.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils keep work and industrial production; Moore sees this left program as reworking civilization rather than abolishing it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Primitivists favour radical decentralization and the break-up of mass society, of which secession is a step.

natural-rulers.rationale: Zerzan stresses foragers' egalitarianism and aversion to rank, and the movement aims to end all power relations.

political-violence-never.rationale: Zerzan says industrial society's elements need to be destroyed and insurrectionary journals back sabotage, though pacifist primitivists prefer nonviolent action.

war-builds-character.rationale: Zerzan presents warfare as an outgrowth of agricultural civilization absent from peaceful foraging life.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred: they reject both religion and the state, so they oppose any union of the two, though separation within a state is not their goal.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion and written law are both counted among the products of domestication and civilization.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Primitivists reject capital as well as the state, so privatized policing is just another structure of coercion.

military-superiority.rationale: They want military apparatus abolished and link organized war to civilization.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Primitivists reject nations and mass society altogether, preferring small face-to-face communities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Primitivists see domestication and civilization, not class conflict, as the driver, faulting Marxism for not questioning production.

equal-outcomes.rationale: They hold up the sharing and egalitarianism of foraging bands as the ideal and see stratification as civilization's product.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: They side with foragers pushed off their lands by agricultural societies, though critics say they romanticize indigenous peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Primitivists condemn civilization's expansion over foragers, but money transfers between states are irrelevant to their goals; the texts do not address it.

civilizational-union.rationale: The ideology is defined by opposition to civilization itself.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Post-left and egoist influences sit alongside an ideal of sharing communities, and the texts do not take a position on self-interest as a moral principle.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject citizenship and coercive obligation alike, preferring free face-to-face community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Zerzan argues domination rests on assuming nature is inferior, and primitivism overlaps with deep ecology.

limit-population.rationale: Zerzan expects population to become quite low and Moore expects it to fall as women escape reproductive roles, but neither supports coercive limits.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: This is the core claim: civilization, and industrial civilization above all, is the root of social and ecological harm.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Primitivists want technology abandoned beyond prehistoric tools, not accelerated.

human-enhancement.rationale: Technological enhancement deepens the alienation from direct, natural existence that primitivism opposes.

algorithmic-government.rationale: It would join technological systems with government, both of which primitivists want abolished.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred: they oppose state surveillance, though digital technology is itself part of the system they reject.

restore-past-order.rationale: They reject civilized progress and look to the pre-agricultural past, though Moore calls it inspiration, not a model to copy.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Moore says primitivism refuses to be a fixed ideology and Perlman rejected '-ist' labels, but the texts do not discuss judging policies.

direct-action.rationale: Primitivists dismiss parties, elections and reformism as part of the system and call for a direct break with civilization.

means-match-ends.rationale: Moore rejects organizations and parties because they reproduce the power relations primitivists want to end, though insurrectionary currents accept sabotage.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The defining goal of primitivism is a return to foraging-band life, which it treats as superior to every civilized way of life.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Abolishing specialization is a core primitivist demand, since it is seen as the root of hierarchy and alienation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Zerzan holds up foragers' sharing as the model, though primitivists reject any system of distributing goods.

production-for-use.rationale: Primitivists oppose production for profit but also reject production and work as such; inferred from their critique of capital and work.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Primitivists are anti-capitalist, but they reject the leftist labor theory and trace exploitation to civilization; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Primitivists reject leftism, parties and any seizure of power, aiming to abolish power relations rather than capture them.

collective-farming.rationale: Primitivists see agriculture itself as the original mistake, so they reject farming in any form.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Zerzan traces war to civilization and agriculture rather than to capitalism alone, but sees capitalism as civilization's warlike latest form; inferred.

taxation-theft.rationale: As anarchists, primitivists treat the state's exactions as coercion, though they reject the property-rights framing of this claim; inferred.

harm-principle.rationale: Primitivists want the state abolished, so they reject its authority to restrict anyone at all rather than endorsing a limit on it; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Primitivists look to face-to-face communal life and treat rights as legal abstractions of civilization; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Primitivists want the military apparatus abolished and see organized war as a product of civilization.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Primitivists dismiss voting as legitimizing the system and favor walking away from civilization's institutions; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Primitivists reject both the state and capital, so modeling government on business deepens both evils.

media-academia-power.rationale: Primitivists criticize mass media and symbolic culture, but locate power in civilization, technology and the state as a whole; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Primitivists stress the shared egalitarian nature of forager humanity and trace inequality to civilization; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Primitivists favor small local communities over parties but reject representation itself in favor of face-to-face life; inferred.

total-state.rationale: Primitivism aims to abolish the state and all power relations.

national-rebirth.rationale: Primitivists seek a return to wildness for humanity, not a national renewal, and reject nations; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Primitivists see expansion and conquest as products of agricultural civilization absent from band life.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Primitivists praise foragers' aversion to rank and want to end all power relations, including ties of lord and follower.

bound-labor.rationale: Zerzan treats domestication and agriculture as the origin of servitude and forced work, which primitivism seeks to end.

universal-morality.rationale: Zerzan distrusts abstract reason and symbolic thought as products of civilization, though primitivists make sweeping moral claims against domination; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Primitivists reject politics and abstract reason in favor of small autonomous bands; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Primitivists want every state abolished, so they deny any people's right to one.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Citizenship presupposes the states primitivists want abolished; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and nations outright, and Zerzan even criticizes symbolic language as part of domestication.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Primitivists reject work, the division of labor and industrial organization itself rather than seeking to democratize large companies; they would abolish rather than co-govern them. Inferred from that rejection of industrial work, not a stated position on codetermination.

school-vouchers.rationale: Primitivists criticize compulsory schooling and the state as instruments of domestication, but a voucher scheme still funds institutional schooling through the state, so an adherent would not endorse it. Inferred from the anti-state, anti-institution critique.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Adherents want the industrial economy and state dismantled, so they have no stake in how its fiscal policy is run, and nothing in the cited sources addresses stimulus or deficits. Treated as genuinely indifferent.

economic-freedom.rationale: Inferred: primitivists see property, trade and work as products of civilization that create unfreedom, so they reject the claim that freedom rests on economic liberty, but they also reject planning and the state rather than endorsing a regulated economy.

rule-by-example.rationale: Inferred from primitivism's rejection of rulers altogether: order is expected to come from small egalitarian communities, not from leaders' example, though it equally rejects laws and punishments.

national-self-determination.rationale: Primitivists want every state abolished, so they deny that nationhood entitles any people to its own state; they prefer small face-to-face bands to nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its military apparatus abolished and see organized war as a product of civilization, so a country using force abroad on its own judgment is rejected, though UN approval is no part of their view.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Zerzan criticizes reason, symbolic thought and rationalism as products of civilization and domination, while also rejecting religion, so they do not make reason the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject the state and its citizenship categories and hold that people should share freely, though they do not defend state welfare either.

positive-liberty.rationale: Inferred: primitivists define freedom as life without domination and reject the industrial economy that would supply the material means.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Zerzan and Moore want work itself abolished and reject the welfare state along with the state that runs it.

class-collaboration.rationale: They reject wage labour and employer-worker relations altogether and dismiss the left and reformism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: they want civilization and its institutions dismantled, and museums and libraries are part of what they oppose, though few address them directly.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: they oppose states and globalization but reject nationalism and leftist anti-imperial fronts as still within civilization.

workers-nation.rationale: They want the state and nations abolished and reject the working-class politics of the left.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Zerzan treats gender division and patriarchy as products of civilization to be overcome, and Moore calls for ending power relations.

ban-interest.rationale: Inferred: they want money and the economy abolished and oppose law enforced by a state, so a legal ban is not their means.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: They oppose the state and all hierarchy, so a state-enforced racial order is rejected.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Inferred: they see the state as an instrument of domination arising from civilization, though they trace it to domestication more than to class alone.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Primitivists want industrial society dismantled and cities and industry abandoned, so expanding fossil extraction runs directly against their aim.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred: they reject nations and the national culture itself as products of civilization, and so any demand to assimilate to it.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: they reject nationalism and the right and blame civilization's structures, not a plot against a native population.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred: they reject the state, parties and electoral reform alike, so none of these electoral systems is their goal.

national-mission.rationale: They want the state abolished and reject nationalism, so no nation has a mission to export its government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Zerzan and Moore trace gender hierarchy and the domination of women to domestication and civilization, and hold it is built into society.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: They see all rulers as part of a system of domination, though they locate the problem in hierarchy itself rather than corrupt individuals.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred: coercive state control over reproduction is the kind of domination they want abolished.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Split: they are hostile to police and military, but also reject the state's courts, so accountability through them is not their route; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They want the state abolished entirely, including the army, courts and police that this statement would keep.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Primitivists reject hierarchy and domination in all forms; inferred from that.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Egalitarianism is core: hunter-gatherer bands are held up as equal, non-hierarchical societies.

socialism-one-country.rationale: They reject state socialism and revolutionary vanguards alike; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: They see colonialism as civilization's expansion that destroys indigenous life; inferred from the critique of civilization.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: They want state law abolished rather than unified, so a common code is not the goal; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Anti-authoritarian, so against legal policing of belief; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: They oppose domestication but also oppose state coercion; inferred, so they would not ban by law.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: They reject state schooling as domestication, so the question of what it should teach is not theirs; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The state is itself part of the problem and should be abolished, not strengthened.

consent-of-governed.rationale: No state has anyone's consent, and the only legitimate authority is voluntary and face to face; inferred from anarchist principles.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Zerzan treats science, language and symbolic culture as tools of domination, in line with the audit's answer on knowledge and power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Primitivists oppose globalization and industrial trade, so a national export goal makes no sense to them.

population-transfer.rationale: Primitivism rejects the state and all coercive hierarchy, so a state removing a minority is rejected.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Primitivists reject domination and coercion but accept sabotage of industrial systems, so an absolute rule is not endorsed; inferred.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Zerzan presents foraging bands as egalitarian and cooperative, and blames competition and domestication for hierarchy.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Primitivists want the state abolished, so they would not grant a state the power to ban parties; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Ending hierarchy and power relations is the core primitivist aim, so unused arbitrary power over a person is itself unfreedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Primitivists want no state at all, so dividing state power is not their remedy; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Primitivists reject parties, leaders and the left's organizational forms, favoring spontaneous decentralized action.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Primitivists want egalitarian bands without institutions or laws, so they neither rank the poor first nor treat all alike; inferred and split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Inferred: home ownership schemes keep people in property and housing under civilization, which primitivists want dismantled.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Inferred: legal labour regulation is a reformist matter within work and the state, which primitivists reject outright.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred: Zerzan treats poverty and scarcity as products of agriculture and civilization, not of foragers' numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject nationalism and hierarchy, and favour small bands over cohesion built on shared ancestry.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Inferred: lotteries still fill state offices, and primitivists want the state and its offices abolished.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Primitivists seek to abolish the state and all power relations, so state emergency powers are rejected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Inferred: price ceilings are state economic management inside civilization, which primitivists oppose.

party-controls-media.rationale: Rejects the state and every power relation; state control of information is exactly what it opposes.

party-commands-army.rationale: Rejects both the state and parties and any standing army; command by a party is doubly opposed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred: citizenship is a state category, and primitivists want states and borders abolished.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject hierarchy and privilege, so officeholders living above ordinary people would be rejected, though they want the offices abolished altogether.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Primitivists reject organizational hierarchy and binding authority; Zerzan favors spontaneous, non-institutional action over party structures.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They oppose the state and large-scale institutions as products of civilization, so a binding supranational union is the opposite of their small face-to-face ideal.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Anarchists reject the state, so no head of state should command forces or choose ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Primitivists reject organized religion and all hierarchy as products of domestication and civilization.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by any authority, clerical included, is rejected by anarchism as a whole.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Anarchists reject the state's claim to loyalty and oppose militarism, so ordinary people owe their rulers no support in wars.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Anarchism opposes state censorship and coercive authority over culture, even though primitivists criticize art as symbolic culture.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred: they reject presidencies altogether, so a rule enabling indefinite tenure is disliked, but the question is not addressed.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred: anarchists favor delegates being revocable at any time, though primitivists reject representation itself.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred: primitivists want the state and its military abolished, which implies ending permanent alliances and foreign garrisons.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Inferred: they reject property and ownership as sources of hierarchy, so a universal homeownership scheme is not their aim either.

people-in-arms.rationale: They oppose standing armies as part of the state, but their wider rejection of institutions and split over violence leaves this unclear.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Primitivists want people to leave cities and live in close contact with nature, seeing urban civilization as alienating.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and national borders, so reunifying a nation into one state runs against their aims.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from their critique of civilization's specialization and symbolic culture, which they see as cutting people off from direct life.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: They treat forager life as better than civilized life, so they would not say cultures are merely different.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred: they reject the state and its coercion, so state executions are opposed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: They support gender equality but reject schooling and the state curriculum, so the statement does not fit their program.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from their critique of institutional schooling and organized religion; no stated position on this debate.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose state coercion yet criticize commodified sexuality in civilization.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its borders abolished, so citizenship of any kind has no place in their program.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred: they value small local communities but oppose state institutions as vehicles for this.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; they reject state law altogether, so exemptions from it are not their framing.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: They see civilization's domestication and social controls as stunting human freedom and favor spontaneous, unregimented life.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject money, debt and the state-led global economy, so debts are illegitimate rather than owed.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: independence as a nation-state changes nothing for primitivists who want the whole economy and civilization dismantled.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred: primitivists want to abolish the state and dismiss institutional reform, so a new constitution is beside the point.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Primitivists reject both state coercion and economic growth, which they see as the engine of civilization's destruction.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred: aid spreads industry and development, which primitivists reject; they favour local self-sufficiency.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Primitivists want the state and industrial technology abolished, so national nuclear arms are the opposite of their aims.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Primitivists reject parties, elections and reformism; direct versus indirect choice is not addressed, so inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred: primitivists want to abolish money, banking and the state that runs them.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject the state and nationalism, so a claim to hold historic land has no standing.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Primitivists reject private property as a source of hierarchy and want things held in common, which goes beyond this claim.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Inferred: anarchists see Soviet industry as a hierarchy of state bureaucrats over wage labor, not socialism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Primitivists oppose industrial technology and its ecological harm, which supports caution, though they want no government to enforce it.

collective-defense.rationale: Primitivists want the state and its military alliances abolished.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Opposed to states and colonization, they would reject conquered territory; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Primitivists reject the state, so it has no authority over anyone, though they also criticize religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Abolition of the state means no head of state, partisan or not.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and its military.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Decentralized small communities with their own ways are favored, though a larger state is rejected; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Primitivists reject hierarchy and rulers, and criticize religion as part of civilization.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Primitivists want states, taxation and money abolished.

character-from-environment.rationale: Zerzan blames civilization for shaping people, implying circumstances matter; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Primitivists reject all rulers and state law.

space-expansion.rationale: Primitivists reject industrial technology and civilization, and treat space expansion as its worst form.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Primitivism rejects rule by any few or many state body.

leader-cult.rationale: Primitivists reject all hierarchy and rulers.

equal-parenting.rationale: Courts are state institutions they reject, so no court presumption; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Primitivists see hierarchy and new elites re-emerging in any state or party revolution, which is why they reject the left and vanguard parties; inferred from that critique.

land-redistribution.rationale: They want agriculture and property abolished, not estates handed to farmers, so redistribution to cultivators is not their remedy; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Anarchists oppose borders and state control of movement, so free return fits; inferred, not a stated primitivist demand.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and nationalism outright, so claiming land for a nationality has no place.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Opposition to coercion, the state and organised religion rules out legal punishment for leaving a faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: They reject state coercion and patriarchy, so a legal dress requirement is opposed.

common-currency.rationale: Money, markets and large-scale institutions are to be abolished, so a shared currency is opposed; inferred from that rejection.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Large political unions cut against their small face-to-face communities and rejection of states; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: They want no state and no formal schooling system, so state-recognised minority institutions are not their model; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Both founding a homeland and seeking state-guaranteed rights rely on states they reject, so this is not their question; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Zerzan locates change in domestication, symbolic culture and alienation, not only production, and primitivists reject the Marxist left; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: They want the economy itself dismantled, not a competitive market preserved by state antitrust action; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: As anti-statists who welcome the collapse of industrial systems, they would not spend public money to rescue them; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They reject representative democracy and majority rule as forms of domination, and institutions of state generally; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for state bodies presuppose a state they want abolished; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: They favour small self-reliant local communities and oppose globalization, but not a state bloc with colonies; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding state treaties on trade are reformism within the globalized system they reject; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Their gift-economy and abolition-of-work vision replaces wages with shared purpose, though they do not frame it as duty; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Moore's Primer rejects vanguard parties and Zerzan expects a mass break, not a small armed group acting for others.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Opposition to all hierarchy and power relations includes rank by birth.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Primitivists reject nation and state as products of civilization and treat written history as civilization's own story, so centring school history on a nation runs against them.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Zerzan and Moore reject progress and hierarchy, and see civilization as the source of domination rather than improvement, so rule in its name is illegitimate.

patriotic-education.rationale: Primitivists want the state abolished and reject schooling as indoctrination; loyalty to a nation and its symbols is the opposite of their stance.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject the state and its admissions and hiring systems wholesale, so the reform question is largely irrelevant to them and offers no clear direction.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred: money and banking, public or private, belong to the civilized economy primitivists want dismantled, so a public issuing body is no solution, though they would not defend private banks.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Primitivists expect industrial civilization to collapse or be broken from its own ecological and social contradictions, and Zerzan treats its crises as terminal.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Primitivists reject empire and state power altogether, so cultivating influence over former imperial territories is a project of domination they oppose.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred: they want all peoples to leave the industrial market, which resembles delinking, but they oppose the development projects delinking theorists usually propose, so the fit is unclear.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject the left's class framing and see all industrial workers as bound into civilization, so the labor-aristocracy thesis is neither endorsed nor clearly rejected.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Primitivists want egalitarian face-to-face communities without hierarchy or domination, and would reject discrimination, while also rejecting the property rights the statement assumes.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Primitivists reject the state and written law as instruments of domination, so a constitutional document that empowers and limits a government has no place.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states and their borders; colonial treaties are not specifically discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Moore's Primer calls for ending power relations and abolishing the state, so rulers of any sort are rejected.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from its anti-coercion, face-to-face egalitarianism; unanimity rules are not stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: they reject all rulers and welcome their removal, though not on constitutional grounds.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Moore's Primer calls for abolishing the state, including its legislatures.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Zerzan's Future Primitive criticizes domestication as a source of suffering for animals as well as people.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Zerzan's account of domestication as the origin of hierarchy leads primitivists to reject keeping animals for use.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: primitivists reject hierarchy and class, so duties of the privileged over the poor are not endorsed.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Zerzan's interviews call for activism against civilization; however, some forms of withdrawal fit, so this is low.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from Zerzan's critique of symbolic culture and technology as tools of alienation and domination.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from Moore's analysis of power relations and technology as systems that maintain the order.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from Zerzan's critique of globalization as extending civilization's domination.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from rejection of the state and of citizenship as a basis of privilege.

party-own-road.rationale: Moore's Primer rejects the left, parties and reformism, so party road to socialism is not part of it.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from Zerzan's call for decentralization and local self-sufficiency; foreign aid is not addressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states and nations; irredentism is not discussed.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from rejection of all political leadership and hierarchy.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from rejecting the state and constitutions altogether; anti-fascism is a stance, not a founding principle.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Zerzan sees all civilization as domination, so the equivalence question is not addressed directly.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from a mainstream critical view of history; not addressed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from rejection of states and national symbols, though preservation is not discussed.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Zerzan's interviews on gender do not address male disadvantage specifically.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from Moore's opposition to domination in family and gender relations.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from the view that civilization imposes its own institutions on all peoples.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Moore's Primer calls for abolishing the state, including its armed forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: Zerzan's Postscript calls for abolishing work, so turning care into paid labour is rejected.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred: Zerzan treats family and kinship obligations as part of the domestication of social life, though band-style kin bonds are valued informally.

office-by-exam.rationale: Primitivists reject hierarchy, specialisation and state institutions, so selecting officials by credentialed exam has no place.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred: they want states and corporations both abolished, so neither side of the policy is attractive, but state action is the more rejected.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the critique of marriage as an institution of domestication; free association without state permission fits.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: they reject representation and delegation altogether in favour of face-to-face communities, so a system of elected leaders is not their model.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Money, capital markets and private companies are all part of the civilization they want dismantled, and pensions presuppose them.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred: they reject private property in land and favour common use by bands, though "nation" ownership is not their language.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: They reject the state and parliaments as institutions, so a budget approval rule is not something they would endorse.

single-official-language.rationale: State-imposed standardisation is part of the domination they oppose, and Zerzan is critical of symbolic culture generally.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred: they reject both property in land and national borders, so a state rule excluding foreigners from owning it is not endorsed.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred: they oppose racism but also reject state legal doctrine, so adherents have no clear position on this test.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Their critique of civilisation holds that commodity culture and alienated work make life worse, and they urge abandoning it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: They reject the state, war and militarism, so a state arming insurgents is contrary to their anarchism.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: They oppose states, armies and domination of one people by another, so great-power invasion of an ally is firmly rejected.

missingStatements.text: Humanity would be better off returning to a hunter-gatherer way of life.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining goal of primitivism is a return to foraging-band life, which it treats as superior to every civilized way of life.

missingStatements.text: The invention of agriculture was a mistake for humanity.
missingStatements.rationale: Zerzan treats the Neolithic turn to farming and domestication as the origin of hierarchy, coercion and ecological ruin.

missingStatements.text: The division of labor should be abolished.
missingStatements.rationale: Abolishing specialization is a core primitivist demand, since it is seen as the root of hierarchy and alienation.

notes: Primitivists split on means: insurrectionary currents (Green Anarchy, Species Traitor) back sabotage, while pacifist primitivists reject violence. Many policy statements assume a state that primitivists want abolished, so the answers to them are inferred and marked low. Kaczynski shares the anti-industrial critique but rejected anarchism and leftism and is excluded.
